description: `notify.py:251-358,603,406` (`_bound_notification`/`_truncate`) caps a notification's title at `TITLE_MAX_CHARS` (250) and its body at `BODY_MAX_BYTES` (4096), replacing whatever was cut with the `…[truncated]` marker, applied inside `send` before the record is queued or pushed. No topic file exists here, so `ntfy_push` short-circuits before any network call (same no-topic path as `notify-no-topic-queues-and-flush`), and the oversized title is still bounded by the time `--flush` prints it back — the CLI-visible proof that the cap runs at queue time, not only at push time (`mv-state::notify`'s own unit tests cover the body/byte-limit side directly, which this command never echoes to stdout).
